Bug_Title: "@Bean" methods for Singleton should not be invoked in "@Configuration" when proxyBeanMethods is false
Bug_Details:
When setting the proxyBeanMethods attribute to false the @Bean methods are not proxied and this is similar
to removing the @Configuration stereotype. In this scenario, @Bean methods within the @Configuration annotated
class operate in lite
mode , resulting in a new bean creation each time the method is invoked.
For Singleton beans, this could cause unexpected outcomes as the bean is created multiple times instead of being created once and
cached.
The rule raises an issue when the proxyBeanMethods attribute is set to false and the @Bean method of a Singleton bean is directly invoked in the @Configuration annotated class code.
Bug_Explanation: This code demonstrates the bug where a Singleton bean is created each time it's invoked from within a @Configuration class. This is because of the proxyBeanMethods attribute being set to false in the @Configuration class.
Trigger_Explanation: The @Bean methods for Singleton should not be invoked in the @Configuration class when proxyBeanMethods is false. In this scenario, the @Bean methods operate in lite mode, resulting in a new bean creation each time the method is invoked. For Singleton beans, this could cause unexpected outcomes as the bean is created multiple times instead of being created once and cached. The bug is triggered when the proxyBeanMethods attribute is set to false and the @Bean method of a Singleton bean is directly invoked in the @Configuration annotated class code.
